purpose: Turn repeated prompt, workflow, validation, review, runtime, and repository hygiene defects into retained regression controls instead of repeated one-off repairs.

recurrence.rule: Two or more independently evidenced occurrences in the same defect family are a system defect. Repairing another instance without strengthening the canonical prevention owner is incomplete.

local_first_proof.semantic_authority: Repository-owned validators, required-check profiles, fixtures, and exact-candidate receipts define the portable merge gate; hosted providers may execute those contracts but do not own their semantics.
rules: When local Git and the repository-owned required-check runner are available, run the local profile before hosted provider proof.
Bind local proof to the exact base/head candidate, invoked profile or command set, exit status, and produced receipt/artifact where the repository supports receipts.

Provider unavailability does not erase valid local proof, but local proof does not grant merge authority when the repository's current promotion contract still requires provider mutation or another external gate.
A local and hosted gate that intend to prove the same invariant must consume the same repository-owned command/profile contract rather than maintain divergent command lists.

repository_hygiene.rule: Patch hygiene is an early local gate, not a late hosted-CI cleanup step. A recurring whitespace failure must strengthen prevention and regression coverage rather than only strip the latest whitespace.

line_ending_policy.rule: Repository line-ending behavior is declared completely in root .gitattributes. Auto-detected text defaults to LF on every platform, listed source/config/docs retain explicit LF controls, Windows command launchers use CRLF, binaries opt out, and no extra active root rule may silently override the contract. Do not mass-renormalize unrelated tracked files merely to introduce this policy.

matrix_boundary: The prompt retrospective matrix is one intake source, not the defect universe. A defect family may be created from local gates, CI, review, runtime, operator feedback, or commit history even when no prompt-use matrix row captures it.
systemic_repair_requirements: A reproducing negative fixture or mutation case demonstrates the defect before the repair.
A positive control demonstrates allowed behavior is preserved.
The smallest canonical shared owner is strengthened; prompt-by-prompt copy edits are rejected when a shared owner exists.
The regression is registered in the deterministic floor when repository convention classifies it as a focused Prompt Kit semantic regression.
Affected local required checks pass before integration when executable in the current environment.
Hosted provider parity is additional proof when applicable, not a replacement semantic owner.
The retained regression remains present after integration.
Prompt semantic coverage incidents must ratchet live operational coverage and effective override bindings instead of treating raw-canonical profile coverage as the whole Prompt Kit.
proof_ceiling: Repository contract and regression semantics only. It can prove that recurring defects are classified, assigned to a canonical owner, regression-tested, and included in repository-owned local proof surfaces. It does not by itself grant hostless merge authority, prove downstream model obedience, or replace provider-only/external gates still required by the active repository promotion contract.

rules: Known unprofiled operational prompt debt may shrink but may not grow; any operational prompt outside the accepted-profile set and outside the reviewed baseline fails closed.

The reviewed known_unprofiled_prompt_ids seed is immutable after establishment; new IDs may never be added to it. Debt reduction is measured from current accepted profiles without rewriting the historical seed.
Every current override prompt must have an explicit baseline binding, critical behavioral markers, and repository-owned focused regression references.
The current override registry Git blob must match the reviewed baseline; an intentional override edit must refresh the coverage baseline in the same reviewed change.
Closeout OR review owner classification is derived from prompt ownership metadata, not incidental wording in proof text, and any owner-set drift requires explicit baseline review.
A coverage ratchet is prevention, not backfill proof: baseline debt remains unprofiled until Prompt Semantic Coverage accepts profiles through its lifecycle.
